title: The Crab in the Blue Cup

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — NATURE, ECOLOGY AND ANIMALS (NAT-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Isola's animals, plants, tides and weather: tide pools and nesting beaches, washed-up rubbish, shrinking clam beds, strange visitors, creatures doing what creatures do, and choices about the island where nobody gets a perfect answer.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks a child aged 5-13)

collection.description: A child finds a hermit crab living in a strange blue cup washed up from the sea: offer it real shells, or leave it be.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has found a hermit crab on the beach, and it isn't living in a shell. It's living in a small blue cup made of plastic, the kind of thing that washes up after storms and that nobody on Isola knows how to make. The crab seems very pleased with it. It drags it proudly across the sand, bonk, bonk, bonk, over every pebble.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) spends the afternoon collecting empty shells of every size and setting them out in a neat row in front of the crab. The crab inspects every single one. It pokes its claws inside. It considers. Then it climbs back into the blue cup and walks off. (subject) is outraged. (friend), who watched the whole thing, says, "Well, it's a very nice cup." The next morning, the cup is lying empty on the sand, and one of the shells is gone.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) decides it's the crab's business where it lives. For days afterward (subject.he/she) keeps spotting it on the beach, the only blue thing for miles, bonking along. (subject.He/she) names it Cup. Nobody can tell where cups like that come from, or why one ended up here. (subject) has decided it doesn't matter. Cup is home.
